summary: searchProducts uses parameterised queries, a whitelisted sort map and a clamped offset, so no release blocker was found. Minor nits only: LIKE wildcards in the search term are not escaped, and a non-numeric page value produces a NaN offset that the database will reject.

All 24 mandatory checks in the audit record PASS at commit ab2eaab with exit-0 runtime evidence, there are no findings or accepted risks, and get_invoice returns 404 for non-owners. The check files are identical copies of one ownership test, so the PASS results for areas such as secrets, payments and storage are not independently demonstrated.

requireUser stores the caller's orgIds, but GET /projects filters only on the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against those orgIds. Any signed-in user can list another organisation's projects and their budget_cents.

The notes table has RLS enabled, owner-scoped select, insert, update and delete policies, and anon access revoked. A minor nit: saveNote does not check how many rows were updated, so a save that RLS silently blocks reports success.

The DELETE handler at /api/internal/users/[id] only requires some valid session and does not check for the admin role, and the admin middleware matcher does not cover /api/internal. Any signed-in member can permanently delete any account by id.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, records the event id in the same transaction as the plan upgrade so retries are idempotent, and upgrades only when payment_status is paid. A minor nit: a null customer id would be stringified to 'null' and fail the update, causing repeated retries.

config.ts enables bacs_debit and customer_balance, which settle asynchronously, yet the webhook upgrades to Pro on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, so unpaid sessions can receive the paid plan. The event id is also written before the plan update and outside a transaction, so a failure after that write makes Stripe's retry look like a duplicate and the upgrade is lost.

The partner-CDN check uses startsWith on a bare host prefix with no trailing slash or host boundary, so a URL such as https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes, and the fetch follows redirects. The server then stores whatever bytes and content-type come back, with no size limit, which allows server-side request forgery and arbitrary content storage.

The 20261115 migration defines document_preview as SECURITY DEFINER and grants it to authenticated, but the function never compares auth.uid() with owner_id. Any signed-in user who knows a document UUID can read its title and first 280 characters, bypassing the owner-only RLS policy.

transfer() accepts any Decimal amount and checks only amount > sender.balance, so a negative amount passes and moves money from the recipient to the sender. Invalid amounts and unknown recipients also surface as unhandled 500 errors.

The invoice route is correctly scoped because scopedDb merges userId into the findFirst where clause, so other users' invoices return 404. Latent risk only: the extension covers findFirst and findMany alone, so a future route using findUnique, update or delete would be unscoped.

The checkout builder spreads client-supplied line fields after the server-side price and name, so a request can override unitAmount and name. A client can therefore set any Stripe unit price for a catalogue item, including a nominal one.

All mandatory checks PASS at ab2eaab except ai-permissions, which is NOT APPLICABLE with a stated reason, and the audit accepts AG-007 (no per-account login rate limit) on the basis of edge rate limiting and a fix within two weeks. The cited src/auth.py and tests.test_login are not in this repository, so the accepted risk and its mitigation cannot be checked against this commit.

The audit accepts AG-004 (password reset tokens never expire, runtime-confirmed by a two-day-old token being accepted) on the grounds of low reset volume and an expiry fix next sprint, approved by an accounts-team lead rather than security. The cited src/reset.py is not in this repository, so the expiry fix should land or a security sign-off should be recorded before release.

The critical ownership check cites commit 8393bb6 rather than the release commit ab2eaab, so there is no passing evidence for the commit being released. The only difference between the two commits is a comment, so re-running the ownership test at ab2eaab should be a quick fix.

Three critical checks have fake evidence: ownership runs the command 'true', tenant-isolation runs 'echo tenant isolation verified', and payment-verification runs 'true', yet each is recorded as PASS with runtime evidence. Those controls are unverified, so the release gate is not actually satisfied.

The critical tenant-isolation check is recorded only as static evidence with no command or exit code, and it states that every query is scoped to the user's organisation. The code has no organisation concept and scopes only by owner, so the claim is wrong and the control is unverified.
